grades.quote: Because programs frequently access the same locations again (that is, exhibit _temporal locality_ ) or access nearby locations (that is, exhibit _spatial locality_ ), the processor will often be able to get its data from the cache rather than from the slower main memory.
grades.reason: Only generic background on cache locality. It explains that caches help when accesses show spatial or temporal locality, so page-strided accesses that lose spatial locality would likely miss. It never mentions page-sized strides, TLBs, or cache conflicts, and its focus is thread switching and processor affinity.
Covers disk locality and request queuing, not in-memory array access, page-stride effects, TLBs, or caches.
Covers races and locking in the xv6 free-page list. It has nothing on slow strided array access or page-distance effects.
